name: Volkswagen Golf GTI
reliability: 7/10 — EA888 is strong and long-lived, but water pump, carbon buildup, and DSG service are watch items
cost_to_own: Insurance: Moderate (practical hot hatch) · Maintenance ~$630/yr (VW parts/labor)
popular_mods: APR / Unitronic / Cobb Stage 1 ECU tune (290-300+ hp)
Lowering springs or coilovers + rear sway bar (tames understeer/torque steer)
oil_interval: Every 5,000-7,500 miles (don't follow VW's 10k LongLife interval)

generations.Mk1 (1976–1983): The original GTI — it invented the hot hatch.
generations.Mk5 (2006–2009): Return to form after the soft Mk3/Mk4 era. 2.0T FSI.
generations.Mk6 (2010–2014): Refined Mk5 on the same platform. 2.0T, widely loved.
generations.Mk7 (2015–2021): EA888 Gen3, 210→228hp (US). Often called the GTI sweet spot — sharp chassis, available manual, analog feel.
generations.Mk8 (2022–present): 241hp EA888 evo4. Quicker but controversial touch-capacitive controls and laggy infotainment. Manual dropped after 2024 in the US.

common_issues: Plastic water pump / thermostat housing cracks and leaks (~50k miles)
Carbon buildup on intake valves (direct injection)
DSG mechatronic/clutch wear if fluid isn't serviced
Mk8 buggy infotainment and frustrating touch controls
maintenance_tips: Replace the plastic water pump/thermostat proactively around 60-80k
Service the DSG fluid every ~40k miles
Use VW 504.00 oil and shorten the LongLife interval to 5-7.5k

engine.detail: 2.0L EA888 evo4 turbo four, 241 hp / 273 lb-ft, running combined direct plus port injection.
engine.watch: The plastic water pump/thermostat housing cracks and leaks, and DI still cakes the intake valves - plan on a walnut blast.

drivetrain.detail: FWD through a 6-speed manual or 7-speed DQ381 wet-clutch DSG, with a VAQ electronically controlled limited-slip diff.
drivetrain.watch: The DSG lasts only if you service its fluid and filter around every 40k; skip it and the mechatronics and clutches wear.

suspension.detail: Struts front, multilink rear with optional DCC adaptive dampers - a genuinely sorted hot-hatch chassis.
suspension.watch: It'll understeer and tug at the wheel when pushed hard; a stiffer rear sway bar sharpens turn-in nicely.

brakes.detail: Vented front discs sized for the ~3,150 lb hatch, with strong, progressive street feel.
brakes.watch: Fine for the road; heavy track use wants better pads and fluid to hold off fade.

electrical.detail: MIB3 infotainment with capacitive touch sliders and steering-wheel touchpads replacing physical buttons.
electrical.watch: Mk8 software is buggy and laggy - glitchy screens, unlit sliders and occasional module gremlins are the real Mk8 gripe.
